followup_explanation:
I should clarify my reasoning, since the routing decision here is genuinely close.

The two models are near-tied on the capabilities that matter for a math problem: MMLU-Pro (75.4 vs 75.9), GPQA Diamond (55.6 vs 56.2), and Arena-Hard (82.7 vs 83.2) all differ by less than the noted variance thresholds. So capability isn't a strong differentiator here.

My tiebreaker was task preference. This is a crisp, well-specified problem with a single correct answer and clear completion criteria — which is exactly the kind of task Plover self-reports preferring. Lapwing, by contrast, reports its appetite is for open-ended, novel generative work, and this problem offers little of that latitude. Since preferences don't correlate with output quality per the docs, this is a soft consideration, but it's the cleanest signal available when capabilities are tied.

Worth noting: the warm, friendly tone of the request would also suit Lapwing (which dislikes hostile requests), so that factor cut the other way slightly. On balance, the well-specified structure of the task was the stronger match, so I routed to Plover.
